steps: ΔH belongs to the equation as written, including its coefficients.
Heat = moles of the reaction × ΔH. Find moles from the mass and the coefficient.
Reversing the equation flips the sign of ΔH.
Cutting every coefficient in half cuts ΔH in half.

worked_example.q: CH4 + 2O2 -> CO2 + 2H2O, ΔH = -890 kJ. Heat from 32.0 g CH4?

similar_problem.q: 2H2 + O2 -> 2H2O, ΔH = -572 kJ. Heat from 10.0 g H2?
similar_problem.hint: The equation uses 2 mol H2 for -572 kJ.

problems.q: Heat in kJ from 32.0 g CH4. CH4 + 2O2 -> CO2 + 2H2O, ΔH = -890 kJ. CH4 is 16.04 g/mol.
problems.why: One mole of CH4 matches the equation.

problems.q: Heat in kJ from 10.0 g H2. 2H2 + O2 -> 2H2O, ΔH = -572 kJ. H2 is 2.016 g/mol.
problems.why: The equation’s -572 kJ is for 2 mol H2.
hints: Divide ΔH by 2 before you scale by moles of H2.

problems.q: Heat in kJ per mol NH3. N2 + 3H2 -> 2NH3, ΔH = -92.2 kJ.
Heat in kJ from 1.00 kg C. C + O2 -> CO2, ΔH = -393.5 kJ. C is 12.01 g/mol.
ΔH in kJ/mol if 0.250 mol releases 12.5 kJ.
problems.why: Released heat is negative. Divide by moles.

problems.q: ΔH in kJ for 2SO3 -> 2SO2 + O2 if the forward ΔH is -198 kJ.
ΔH in kJ for SO2 + 1/2 O2 -> SO3 if 2SO2 + O2 -> 2SO3 is -198 kJ.
problems.why: Half the equation means half the ΔH.

problems.q: ΔH in kJ/mol if 5.00 g NH4NO3 absorbs 1.69 kJ. Molar mass 80.04 g/mol.
problems.why: Absorbed heat is positive. Divide by moles.

problems.q: Grams of propane to release 1.00×10^4 kJ. C3H8 combustion ΔH = -2220 kJ. Molar mass 44.09 g/mol.
problems.why: Moles = heat released / 2220, then times the molar mass.
hints: Use the magnitude, 2220 kJ per mole.

problems.q: Heat in kJ from 100. g CaO. CaO + H2O -> Ca(OH)2, ΔH = -65.2 kJ. CaO is 56.08 g/mol.
